entities.name: Mathias Sommerhielm
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mathias Sommerhielm (1769–1824) was a Norwegian jurist and statesman who served as Minister of Justice of Norway (1814–1822) — one of the most critical offices in the new Norwegian constitutional state created by the Eidsvoll Constitution of May 1814. As the first Minister of Justice, he helped build the judicial and legal administrative infrastructure of the newly constitutional Norwegian state during the most formative years of Norwegian self-governance.

The Norwegian Constitution of 1814 — created in response to the dissolution of the Danish-Norwegian union following Napoleon's defeat and Denmark's cession of Norway to Sweden — was one of the most liberal constitutions in early nineteenth-century Europe. Despite the subsequent forced union with Sweden, Norway retained its constitution and Storting (parliament), and its national institutions — including the Ministry of Justice that Sommerhielm led — had genuine autonomy.

His eight-year ministerial tenure (1814–1822) covered the entire critical first phase of Norwegian self-governance under the new constitutional order.

He was among the most important architects of modern Norwegian governance.
